ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the central angle $\angle AOB$ is $100^\circ$. What is the measure of the inscribed angle $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let point E be a point on the major arc AB, and connect EA and EB. \\
$\because$ $\angle$AOB=100$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$E= $ \frac{1}{2}\angle$AOB=50$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACB=180$^\circ$−$\angle$E=\boxed{130^\circ}.

According to the inscribed angle theorem, an inscribed angle equals half the measure of the arc it subtends, so ∠ACB=260°÷2=130°.

Read from the text that the central angle ∠AOB is 100°. Since ∠AOB subtends the minor arc AB, that minor arc has measure 100°. The inscribed angle ∠ACB has its vertex C on the minor arc AB, so it intercepts the opposite major arc AB, whose measure is 360°−100°=260°. By the inscribed angle theorem, ∠ACB is half its intercepted arc, so ∠ACB=130°.
